§7.3.3 Handwritten Annotations

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

text-handwritten-annotations · text marks handwriting

✅ Normative

A handwritten note on a printed page MUST be rendered as [handwritten: legible words], in a block of its own next to the content it annotates. Its legible words MUST be kept; words that cannot be read MUST NOT be reconstructed.

A note written on a printed page: an exhibit reference in the margin, a circled item, an arrow with a word, a reviewer's initials. Handwriting and Stamps§9.6.5 settles handwriting that replaces a printed value inside a table; a note in the margin of prose replaces nothing.

    … to confirm the absence of cyclonic flow.

                                      2                     Attach. B   ← red pen
                                                       SAQB 193        ← Bates stamp

Requirements

  • The note adds information to the printed page, so it MUST be kept, and MUST be kept apart from the body text: it MUST NOT be spliced into the sentence beside it.
  • The block MUST sit next to the content the note annotates in reading order.
  • Legible fragments MUST be kept verbatim. Characters that cannot be read are left out, never guessed.

✅ Sample — an exhibit reference in red pen

Attach. B handwritten in red at the bottom right of a scanned protocol page, beside a printed Bates number SAQB 193. The page's own number, 2, is centred above.
